tasks.title: Prime-cover reduction: correctness and full-cost review
tasks.brief: Review the mathematical relaxation in H004: only every prime<=R=floor(sqrt N) is covered by nonzero leaves A_i, a modular interval-product routine is available, and a costed routine resolves prime divisors of gcd(d,A_i). Establish precisely whether these conditions suffice for full factorization including repeated factors, gcd=N branches, a prime remainder, and all preprocessing. Compare Umans–Wang Theorem 5.2: is the relaxation new, implicit, or useless? Identify noncircular implementations of the leaf primitive or prove a precise obstruction for a proposed restricted implementation. Do not replace the primitive with an oracle. Deliver an explicit conditional proposition and proof/counterexample, complete cost recurrence, limitations, and one decisive next step. Focus on correctness/cost, not broad new ideation.

tasks.title: Prime-cover construction: one concrete family and falsifier
tasks.brief: Investigate ONE concrete, uniformly describable prime-only difference-cover family under H004. Start from the shifted arithmetic progression option in Umans–Wang Section 6 or a materially different explicit family, but do not just survey. Attempt a construction or a rigorous cost/coverage obstruction. If finite search is useful, preregister parameters and rejection criterion in your report before running a capped <=60-second script. All construction work is charged; no giant primorial, factors of N, hidden universal lookup or unpriced leaf factoring. Compare actual required height, set size, description length, and prime coverage; finite wins do not imply an asymptotic family. Include the largest missed primes/negative cases and a next revision if the first design fails. You may write uniquely prefixed H004-cover- scratch/evidence files next to your report.
